# Agriculture in Seminole County, Florida

In the 1920s, agriculture in Seminole County, Florida expanded significantly, especially in celery and other vegetables.
This growth was fueled by increasing demand from northern markets and improvements  rail transportation. The agricultural boom attracted many migrant farm workers to the area, many of whom were African American, who settled near the fields. Their presence helped establish communities such as Midway.
Complications
Despite regional economic growth, many area continued to face challenges, such as long labour shortages, and housing affordability pressures that constrained broader development.
